key_insight: The paper replaces POD modes with a feature-based manifold and augmented state space to predict transient bluff-body wake dynamics under arbitrary time-varying actuation.
engineering_relevance: This offers an interpretable reduced-order surrogate for control-oriented flow prediction, useful for actuator design and real-time wake management in bluff-body systems.
method: Build a feature-based manifold with the same dimension as the original POD space
Distill the state from dynamic features that represent coherent structures over time
Augment the state space to capture transient response to time-varying actuation
evidence_signal: Validated on the fluidic pinball at Re=30 across several representative actuation scenarios, where it reproduces transient dynamics without unsteady training data.
watch_item: The model is demonstrated on a canonical low-Re configuration, so broader robustness and scaling to more complex flows still need verification.
paper_title: Feature-based manifold model of actuated wakes
